units.function: Runs the interactive configuration editor for database, LLM, logging, server/auth, storage and Secret-provider sections. It reads the existing config, warns while preserving unknown keys, backs up invalid bytes, requires interactive repair confirmation, updates one selected section at a time, manages the local Secret key file and persists after each section.
units.dependencyDirection: configure command -> config store/schema/home/Secret-key modules and section-specific prompt modules -> filesystem/config and optional environment master key. Product defaults and operational policy are assembled in the CLI, while field validation, atomic write behavior and permissions belong to separately audited config modules.
units.keyDataModels: PaperclipConfig v1 metadata; embedded PostgreSQL and backup schedule; file logging; local_trusted/private/loopback server; auth base URL and sign-up flag; telemetry enabled; storage and Secret provider configuration; instance-scoped default paths and invalid-config backup path.
units.lifecycle: Require an existing config -> read/validate and warn on unknown keys -> on invalid bytes create a backup and require interactive repair -> choose one section -> run its prompt -> optionally create/reuse a local Secret key -> stamp metadata -> atomically persist through writeConfig -> repeat. Each accepted section commits independently, so later cancellation or failure does not roll back earlier sections.
units.testAssessment: The already completed focused test assessments were reused without rereading source: application:cli/__tests__/configure passed 3/3 and proved fail-closed invalid-config preservation while identifying malformed-byte log leakage and missing success/policy coverage; application:cli/__tests__/configure-repair passed 1/1 and proved confirmation plus atomic commit while leaving field repair, decline/cancel, diff, failure rollback, concurrency and identity/Secret rebinding untested. CLI TypeScript checking passes.
units.designRationale: Interactive section editing reduces accidental full-file replacement, unknown-key preservation supports forward-compatible extensions, invalid-byte backup plus non-interactive refusal is safer than silent repair, and per-section persistence limits the amount of staged in-memory configuration. Local Secret-key bootstrap supports self-hosted operation without an external vault.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs one configuration model and guided setup for managed-cloud and self-hosted/local-enterprise profiles, with independently replaceable identity, database, storage, Connector/model, Secret and telemetry adapters. Repair and migration must preserve extensions and never silently change security or responsibility semantics.
units.companyOsFit: Adapt the preservation, backup and section-editor patterns behind a typed versioned Company OS ConfigPort. Add preview/diff, profile policy validation, migration plans, restrictive backup/key permissions, transactional multi-resource changes, stable error codes and explicit telemetry/data-export consent. Keep environment-specific prompts outside core/application.
units.responsibilityConflict: Defaults enable telemetry and sign-up while identity/telemetry are not first-class selectable sections here. Configuration changes are attributed only to metadata source=configure, not a verified human/operator with reason and evidence. Secret key creation can occur before config persistence, and multi-section edits are partial commits rather than one accountable change set.
evidence: Completed focused assessment application:cli/__tests__/configure: 3/3 passed; REJECT as sufficient proof
Completed focused assessment application:cli/__tests__/configure-repair: 1/1 passed; ADAPT pattern
units.securityFindings: Invalid bytes are backed up before repair consent and parser errors can include original content; backup permissions and redaction are security-critical. Arbitrary config paths, environment-provided master keys and local key creation must be enforced by lower layers. The Secret key may be created before writeConfig succeeds, leaving an orphan. Default telemetry is opt-out, configuration has no displayed diff or human audit event, and each section commits separately. Unknown-key preservation is positive but also means extensions require namespace/schema ownership to prevent policy bypass.
